findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed ice accumulation in the walk-in freezer (Freezer 1). This ice accumulation is contacting bagged vegetables stored on the top shelf in the walk-in. The head of maintenance was present during the inspection and stated that Henson Robinson has performed maintenance on the freezer in the last four weeks. There was thermal tape and insulation foam present on the leaking lines. It seems these fixes are inadequate to prevent leakage onto food and food contact surfaces. The staff were instructed to move the vegetables stored directly below the leaking lines to a dry location and keep a container under the lines to capture the water. Ensure food is stored in clean, dry locations at all times to prevent contamination. The freezer requires maintenance prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Mop basin was observed to be in need of resealing or re-caulking.  Areas subject to moisture must be non-absorbent and easily cleanable.  Ensure mop basin is re-caulked to prevent mold growth.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Walk-in cooler containing milk cartons was observed to contain an accumulation of dust on the cooler fans and grates.  Ensure fans and grates are cleaned regularly to prevent contamination of food items in the walk-in cooler.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16 (P) Shredded mozarrella and cheddar cheese inside a fridge in the serving area was probed at 55 degrees. Thermometers provided inside the fridge were reading close to 50 degrees on both sides. Exterior thermometer was reading at 41.5 degrees. Fridge contained shredded cheese, shredded lettuce, whole tomatoes, and condiments. These items were prepared for lunch service less than an hour prior, and are there only for convenience purposes during lunch service. PIC stated that this equipment has been known to go out of temp sometimes and this is not unusual. PIC removed the prepped items and transferred them to walk-in cooler. PIC also called service technician to service fridge. In the meantime, PIC ceased use of this equipment. Corrected on site.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.citation_text: 3-602.11  (C) Prepackaged cookies are not properly labeled. Label with: 1) common name of food, 2) ingredients, 3) net quantities, 4) name and address of packager, 5) food allergens, 6) nutrition labeling, 7) salmonid fish additives used. Reference 3-602.11.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment: 6-501.110  (C) Employees were found not using the designated dressing rooms / changing areas or designated employees lockers when changing clothes or storing personal articles. Dressing rooms and lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used if employees regularly change clothes or store personal articles in the establishment while working. Reference 6-501.110.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.14  (C) [Intake air / Exhaust air ducts (vents)] in the grill area were found with accumulation of dust on them. Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed a soiled, wet wiping cloth stored on the counter top between uses. Store wiping cloths in sanitizer solution at a proper concentration between uses.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed an open box of single service sandwich wrappers stored below soiled oven mitts. Do not store soiled items above single service items. Properly cover all single service items to prevent possible contamination. Gloves were removed to a proper location to correct the violation. 
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: The ice machine in the concession stand has a light build up on the right side. Also the fan in the dish area has some dust build up on it.  750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use and any time they may have become contaminated. Clean these items.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed utensils improperly stored in drawer with non-food contact and food contact surfaces intermingled. Store utensils with food contact surfaces facing the same direction in the drawer.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
The following floors are soiled:
(a) back corner of dry storage room (possibly droppings), 
(b) underneath shelves in dry storage room (especially close to wall/coving) (possibly droppings),
(c) underneath dish machine and adjacent stainless steel counter tops (possibly droppings under pipes, in corner).

findings.title: Clean and soiled linen segregated and properly stored.
findings.comment:
Multiple damp wiping cloths were piled up in dish area hand sink.  CORRECTED - cloths were immediately hung to dry around rim of soiled laundry receptacle.  Make sure all staff understand that cloths should not be piled in hand sink and should always be placed into designated soiled laundry place.

750-1380b Soiled clothes and linens shall be stored in non-absorbent containers or washable laundry bags until removed for laundering. Properly store soiled linens.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
In the concession stand area, the floor under the ice machine, and the floor under the ice cream machine, are soiled with three or four mouse droppings.  Properly clean and sanitize these surfaces and watch closely for evidence of pests.  Kitchen manager states the pest control operator was here on Friday and reported no pest activity.  There is no evidence of pests elsewhere in facility.  It does not appear there is a pest issue, but the aforementioned floors should be thoroughly cleaned and monitored for new droppings.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Wash, rinse water clean, proper temperature
findings.comment:
Dish machine wash temperature was 138 - 140 degrees F.  Dish machine was running through multiple cycles as inspector approached.  Wash Cycle thermometer never raised above 140.  Machine is labeled stating that Wash Temperature should be 160 degrees F and Rinse Temperature 180.  (It appears that either the machine's thermometer is broken, or the machine is not reaching proper wash temperature.  Either way, the Rinse Cycle appears to be adequate, as that thermometer registered 186 degrees F.)  Manager is calling EcoLab for repair.  Make sure that machine reaches proper temperatures and/or that the thermometers work properly.
750-830 Machines using hot water for sanitizing may be used provided that wash water and pumped rinse water be kept clean and water shall be maintained at not less than the temperature stated for that machine. Single-tank, stationary rack, dual-temperature: wash temperature 150°F.  Single-tank, stationary-rack, single-temperature machine:  wash temperature 165°F.  Single-tank, conveyor machine wash temperature: 160°F.  Multi-tank, conveyor machine wash temperature: 150°F.  Multi-tank, conveyor machine pumped rinse temperature: 160°F.  Single-tank, pot, pan and utensil washer (either stationary or moving rack): wash temperature 140°F.

750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited

Numerous live ants were seen near the area behind the tilt skillet (Bertha). The ants were crawling on the floor and behind the metal paneling.  A page was sent to the pest control company to come inspect and control the situation. A follow up inspection will be done on 9/12/2011.
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Hole was observed in the floor to wall joint behind the tilt skillet (aka Bertha). Inspector was able to stick a pen down in to the hole. Junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch. Repair the hole and check the floor to wall joints throughout the entire facility. Repair any other issues observed. B) Old mouse droppings were observed on the floor/glue trap under can rack. Floors also had general soil in dish and prep areas along the walls behind equipment. C) Floor drain by fryers was soiled down inside. Clean the floors and the drain in the above areas. Keep floors and drains clean.
